stories.title: dtc_freeze_frame sync: quarantine unresolvable cross-tier rows after N failures (stop silent infinite retry)
acceptance: Atlas invariant 1 -- after N consecutive identical cross-tier resolution failures on the same record, the sync loop quarantines it (dead-letter table or data_quality flag) and stops re-attempting every cycle
Atlas invariant 2 -- the raw freeze-frame record is PRESERVED (never dropped) when quarantined; quarantine throttles re-resolution, it does not discard data
Atlas invariant 3 -- the quarantine event is surfaced exactly once (log/alert), not per-cycle
Atlas invariant 4 -- quarantine is re-drainable (throttled/retryable, NOT terminal): once the resolution target exists (e.g. US-367 lands), the record re-enters the queue and syncs
a quarantined record does NOT advance sync_log.last_synced_id and does NOT block other tables/records from syncing
Typecheck passes; tests pass; a test proves N-failures -> quarantine -> single surfacing -> re-drain

validationCriteria.action: simulate an unresolvable cross-tier row for N+1 cycles
validationCriteria.outcome: quarantined after N; surfaced once; no per-cycle re-fail

validationCriteria.action: after quarantine, query the source table for the offending freeze-frame record
validationCriteria.outcome: the raw record still exists (preserved, not deleted)

validationCriteria.action: make the resolution target resolvable then re-run
inspect sync_history during the unresolvable window
validationCriteria.outcome: no unbounded identical-failure spam after quarantine

conditionalOutcomes: if the chosen mechanism needs a NEW CROSS-TIER TABLE (A-4-family versioned-contract change), route to Atlas for a ruling BEFORE coding -- per his 2026-06-28 quick-read a data_quality flag is Ralph-pickable, a new cross-tier dead-letter table is the architectural case
stories.goal: As the sync subsystem, I want a single unresolvable freeze-frame to stop retrying forever (it ran 27x/day for 3+ weeks with no dead-letter/quarantine/alert -- a silent infinite loop that would mask a REAL sync failure in the noise). 'Fail loudly, no silent re-resolve' is correct per-attempt but wrong at the queue level. After N consecutive identical resolution failures, quarantine the record (dead-letter table OR data_quality flag -- Atlas quick-read requested) and surface it ONCE. General safety net; US-367 self-heals the current specific orphan.
